description: Designing systems that start, check and re-run agents toward a goal with little human prompting: trigger, action, verifier, stop rule, persistent state and escalation.
What starts an iteration: a schedule, an event (CI failure, new issue) or the previous iteration's result.
The conditions that end a loop: verified success, stuck output, a failure limit or an exhausted budget.
Stopping when the agent repeats an output that already failed, instead of paying for the same answer again.
Handing an unfinished task to a human with the reason and the full state: attempts, feedback and money spent.
A trigger keyed by its subject, so repeated deliveries continue or return the existing run instead of starting a new one.
Running the same prompt in a fresh agent session in an endless loop, with a plan file and tests as memory and feedback; a minimal loop without stop rules.
Agents run the inner loop (attempt, verify, retry); humans own the outer loop: which loops exist, what done means, the limits and the review.
